title: A review of uphill and downhill running: biomechanics, physiology and modulating factors
claims: Downhill running relies heavily on eccentric muscle contractions, which are associated with greater fatigue and a higher injury risk than level running.
Forefoot striking reduces peak impact forces compared with rearfoot striking, especially in downhill running.
Adjusting cadence can reduce per-step load and energy expenditure during both uphill and downhill running.
